# `liber:admin@1`

Generated reference for the `liber:admin` package (`admin.lsidl`). See [the LSIDL language](../../../LSIDL.md).

LiberSystem administrative authorization - one person's confirmation, on a protected screen, of one bound high-risk operation, and at most one attempt at it.  A REQUEST IS NOT AUTHORITY. A component PermissionManager granted `admin-request` holds a request connection bound to the task it was launched as. It asks for an action on a target; the executor that owns the target resolves and freezes the exact operation - target instance and generation, parameters, payload length and digest - and AdminService waits for a person. Nothing a requester sends is identity: its label is shown as its own words, escaped, beside the canonical operation the service renders itself.  A PERSON DECIDES, ON A SCREEN NOTHING ELSE CAN DRAW. Ctrl+Alt+F12 on the trusted keyboard always enters an OS-owned protected screen; the display is locked to it and the trusted keyboard reports to AdminService alone. Only a fresh Enter after every key was released approves; Escape declines. Refusal, timeout, contention and an unavailable path are all the same `declined`.  A GRANT IS ONE ATTEMPT. A granted request answers a channel served by its grant record. `execute` takes no argument - the operation is the one that was confirmed - and the first call consumes the grant; a second, an expired one, or one whose launching task has ended reaches no executor. A lost reply is `outcome-unknown` and is never retried.  EVERY DECISION IS RECORDED FIRST. Requests and approvals are committed to the service's journal before a grant exists, consumption before the effect is dispatched, and every decline is recorded.

## Types

### resource `admin-payload`

Bytes a requester hands over for an operation. The executor copies what it needs when it prepares, so whatever the requester can still write through its own alias changes nothing that was confirmed.

An opaque kernel object, transferred as `handle<admin-payload>`.

### interface `admin-executor`

THE EXECUTOR CONTRACT, which an `admin-executor` publication serves to AdminService alone. Preparation freezes the operation; revalidation checks it is still the same live target; execution is at most one attempt, under the executor's own start guard.

Request `[op u16][corr u32][args]`, reply `[corr u32][result]`.

| op | method | signature | description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `prepare` | `prepare(action: admin-action, target: string, parameters: list<u8>, payload-length: u32, payload: handle<admin-payload>) -> result<admin-prepared, error>` |  |
| 2 | `revalidate` | `revalidate(operation: u64) -> result<unit, error>` |  |
| 3 | `execute` | `execute(operation: u64, epoch: u64) -> result<admin-result, error>` |  |
| 4 | `cancel` | `cancel(operation: u64) -> result<unit, error>` |  |
